decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm approach to the grapes in the right workspace, lifting slightly and rotating toward a top-down grasp; left arm stays parked.

Continue gradual forward and inward right-arm motion with open fingers, increasing downward wrist pitch while preserving the accepted configuration.
Advance the open right gripper toward the grapes while gradually pitching downward, keeping clearance above surrounding objects.
Move forward above the table toward the target, continuing the smooth top-down orientation change with the right gripper open.
Raise the wrist for fingertip clearance while finishing the overhead approach; table and grape height remain uncertain from the head view.
Replan from the single executed step using smaller increments, retaining fingertip clearance and continuous elbow-up motion.
Use the head and wrist views to shift the right gripper leftward toward the grapes and forward slightly, raising for clearance as it approaches vertical.

Center the raised, open right gripper over the grapes' new visible location, completing the near-vertical orientation without crossing the arms.
The centering chunk was interrupted after one step. Use smaller inward shifts with a slight retreat to retain reach margin while finishing downward alignment.
Bring the open jaws toward the grapes' visible center with a small forward and downward correction; approach depth is still uncertain, so use short increments.
The last forward step was rejected near the reach limit. Lower the open wrist with almost no forward motion to restore extension margin before refining the grasp.
Refine the open-jaw alignment slightly left and forward while descending slowly; use the next RGB view to check whether the cluster is between the fingers.
The cluster appears between the open jaws in the head view. Stop the interrupted approach and close the right gripper in place; retention remains to be checked visually.
Keep the right gripper closed and perform a short upward-and-back lift test, retracting to preserve extension margin; check whether the grapes follow.
The lift test shows empty closed fingers and grapes remaining on the table. Reopen and approach slightly farther forward and lower for a deeper grasp.
The wrist view still places the grapes ahead of the finger tips. Advance the open gripper farther forward while lowering conservatively to maintain reach margin.
The grapes now fill the region between the right fingers in the wrist view. Close at this deeper position without further descent, then verify retention during lifting.
Test the deeper grasp with a controlled four-centimeter lift and slight retraction, keeping the right gripper fully closed and watching whether the cluster follows.
The fingers again lifted empty. Reopen and tilt the grasp slightly forward while lowering modestly, to reach the cluster's center without extending the arm farther.
Advance the angled, open fingers into the center of the cluster with small forward/downward steps, keeping elbow-up continuity and more reach margin.
Hold the angled grasp height and advance another small distance so the jaws surround the cluster's middle rather than its near edge.
Close the angled right jaws around the cluster at the farther-forward position, holding the wrist still to avoid pushing during closure.
Lift the newly closed angled grasp gently upward with slight retraction. Keep the gripper at zero and use the RGB views to determine whether the grapes move with it.
The grapes now remain fixed between the fingers as the wrist rises. Continue lifting with gentle retraction and the right gripper closed, toward more than ten centimeters total lift.
The cluster remains visibly retained above the table. Raise another four centimeters with slight retraction to exceed the ten-centimeter lift requirement while keeping the grip closed.
